symptom: LVS mismatch: missing, shorted, or open nets

first_checks.check: Open LVS detailed report and isolate short isolator vs open locator sections, sort by net with highest mismatch count
first_checks.why_first: cheapest, tells instantly if single global power short dominates vs many local opens

first_checks.check: Compare top-level LVS vs each child block LVS standalone to see if mismatch reproduces in block or only at parent stitching
first_checks.why_first: rules out the most, localizes root to block interior vs hierarchical boundary

first_checks.check: Highlight suspect net in layout viewer and verify text label attachment, pin text layer, and port property vs schematic pin list
first_checks.why_first: cheapest fix, rules out labeling error before chasing metal

discriminating_experiments.experiment: Move or delete suspected text label by order of microns and re-extract; if short disappears, restore label on correct text layer with single attachment point and re-run
discriminating_experiments.rules_in: text label short causing two distinct nets to be merged by label

discriminating_experiments.experiment: Run connectivity trace from schematic port down through hierarchy; if trace stops at a hierarchical port, run that block alone and diff its extracted port list against parent instantiation pins
discriminating_experiments.rules_in: hierarchical pin mismatch or missing property at boundary causing open
discriminating_experiments.rules_out: intra-block metal open or via stack break

discriminating_experiments.experiment: Rerun extraction with fill, dummy metal, and seal ring layers excluded vs included; if open/short disappears when excluded, re-include layers one by one
discriminating_experiments.rules_in: fill tie, seal ring, or dummy bridging causing short or masking open

discriminating_experiments.experiment: Toggle soft-connect and virtual-connect handling for well taps and substrate ties and re-run LVS; if signal net that was shorted to power becomes clean, inspect tap cell placement
discriminating_experiments.rules_in: tap cell or well tie virtual connect merging power with signal

common_root_causes.cause: Text label on wrong layer or label polygon overlapping two separate metal shapes causing virtual short
Floating shape or incomplete via stack at top-level integration leaving intentional open, often after manual edit
Hierarchical port mismatch, missing pin, or off-grid port property so parent does not stitch child net
Real metal short from sliver overlap or DRC-clean but LVS-dirty manual routing
Soft-connect handling of tap cells or guard rings merging signal net to power/ground

classic_trap: Assuming a reported short is a real metal short and spending hours fixing routing, when it is a text label short merging two nets in extraction
node_era_note: At 28nm opens were mostly missing via stacks; at 7nm-and-below color violations from multi-patterning and cut-metal / local interconnect opens and shorts dominate, and via enclosure rules make soft-connect shorts more frequent

symptom: LVS mismatch: wrong device sizes or extra devices

first_checks.check: Check LVS property error table for systematic scaling: are all W/L off by order of 2x or integer finger count vs random values
first_checks.why_first: cheapest, distinguishes folding/merging setting error from random draw error

first_checks.check: List extra devices by type and location: are they all same flavor clustered near fill boundary or scattered
first_checks.why_first: rules out the most, tells if filter issue vs genuine extra layout

first_checks.check: Verify PDK version, LVS deck version, and schematic netlister options match between layout and schematic runs
first_checks.why_first: rules out version mismatch which causes wholesale size mismatches before inspecting individual devices

discriminating_experiments.experiment: Rerun with series/parallel device merging disabled vs enabled and with merging threshold swept; if wrong size or extra count disappears when merging is off or threshold changes, compare netlister merging setting to LVS deck
discriminating_experiments.rules_in: inconsistent series/parallel merging or finger folding between schematic netlister and layout extractor
discriminating_experiments.rules_out: true drawn size error or real extra device

discriminating_experiments.experiment: Overlay marker layers for Vt flavor, thick-oxide, and low-Vt/high-Vt implants on mismatched devices and compare to schematic device flavor; re-extract after correcting marker
discriminating_experiments.rules_in: missing or extra flavor marker causing wrong device type counted as size mismatch or extra device
discriminating_experiments.rules_out: schematic parameter or CDF callback error

discriminating_experiments.experiment: Run LVS with dummy fill, decoupling cap, antenna diode, and ESD device filtering excluded vs included; if extra devices vanish when filtered, check filter options in deck
discriminating_experiments.rules_in: dummy fill, decap, or antenna diode counted as real device
discriminating_experiments.rules_out: unintended physical transistor drawn in layout

common_root_causes.cause: Folding mismatch: schematic uses single large W device while layout uses multiple fingers, netlister folds differently than extractor
Missing or mis-drawn Vt flavor or thick-oxide marker causing LVS to recognize wrong device type or wrong effective size
Series/parallel merging thresholds inconsistent between schematic netlister and LVS deck causing summed W/L to differ
Dummy fill transistors, ESD clamps, or antenna diodes not excluded by LVS filter options
CDF callback or model parameter not propagating W, L, fingers, or m-factor from schematic to netlist, or scale factor applied twice

classic_trap: Chasing layout W/L as drawn wrong and editing layout, when schematic netlist has wrong effective W due to folding or callback and layout is actually correct
node_era_note: At 28nm size is continuous W/L; at 7nm-and-below size is quantized to fins and fingers, and gate-cut and source-drain epi merge rules create systematic extra device and fin-count mismatches not seen at 28nm
